item.title: Trump says 'we don't need a deal with Iran' and that Vance should focus on Democrats
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
By Bo Erickson WASHINGTON, Nov 12 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump said on Thursday the US does not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice President JD Vance, who has played a role in efforts to resolve the war, to focus "his complete ‌and total attention" on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states. Trump's directive came a day after the Wall ‌Street Journal reported that Vance was considering face-to-face peace talks with a hard-line Iranian security official and a week after the vice president blamed the costly war with ​Iran for Republicans' midterm elections drubbing. "We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We’ve got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we’ve got their Strait!" Trump wrote on social media, referring to the Strait of Hormuz. Trump had suggested in recent weeks that Iran would be more willing to strike a deal in the eight-month conflict after the US elections, but his administration this week ‌signaled it believes its blockade and economic sanctions ⁠against Iran are working, meaning neither a military escalation nor diplomacy is needed. The US military is imposing a blockade on Iranian ports, while attempting to secure safe passage for international shipping through the vital Strait of Hormuz. ⁠Iran's military said on Thursday four oil tankers were hit by explosions after they ignored Iranian warnings. Vance's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. VANCE HAD LED IRAN DIPLOMACY Vance, long seen as skeptical of the war the US and Israel launched on Iran in February, led talks with Iranian officials ​in ​Pakistan in April that produced a June memorandum of understanding that paused ​the war but broke down within weeks. Iranian state media said ‌late last month Tehran had received a letter from Vance seeking renewed talks with Washington. Trump said he had not directed his vice president to make the outreach. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Tuesday after talks with US allies in Paris that Iran's demands for a potential deal were "absurd," citing its demand for reparations for the war, and said Trump would not sign a bad deal. The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Vance was considering meeting with a senior Iranian security official, a move that would have put Vance at the ‌center of peace negotiations. Reuters has not confirmed the potential talks. Vance, who is ​viewed as a leading contender for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination, distanced himself ​from the war last week after Republicans' midterm election rout ​by Democrats. The vice president blamed the costs of the Iran war in part for the party's losses. He ‌also said an earlier recommendation to end the war ​was "sound advice." Trump responded to Vance's position ​by defending the war as necessary to stop Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. In his social media post, Trump said he had asked Vance to focus instead on a domestic issue the president previously put in his portfolio: leading an effort targeting alleged ​fraud in Democratic-run cities and states throughout the ‌US. "Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large-scale criminal activity. CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership’s ​blood!" Trump wrote on Thursday. (Reporting by Bo Erickson in Washington; additional reporting by Simon Lewis, Doina Chiacu and Susan ​HeaveyEditing by Colleen Jenkins, Andrea Ricci, Don Durfee and Nia Williams) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/trump-says-vance-focus-domestic-133908907.html

item.title: Van Hollen takes on Schumer for majority leader after Democrats flip Senate
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
WASHINGTON (AP) — Democratic Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland said Thursday that he will run for Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress, setting up a challenge to Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer after the party swept to power in the midterm elections. Van Hollen said in a statement that “the American people called for change” and that is why he is running. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership,” Van Hollen said. “This is not about any one person — it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority Leader.” Schumer has said he has the necessary support to win the race, which will be the first contested election for Senaet Democratic leader in decades. The closed-door, secret-ballot election will be held in early December. The question of whether to reelect Schumer has already divided the caucus and many senators have declined to say publicly how they will vote, even before Van Hollen entered the race. They have privately deliberated about what message to take from the election and many are torn — Schumer recruited many of the party’s winning candidates and raised money for them, but progressive groups are pushing for his removal. Making the pitch for his reelection, Schumer has been working with Democratic senators one-on-one to form an agenda for 2027. In private caucus meetings this week, Schumer opened discussion on a broad plan for their first 100 days in power that included health care and tariff legislation and efforts to stop the Iran war. “I’m going to win it,” Schumer told The Associated Press in an interview last week. In a statement after Van Hollen’s announcement, Schumer said he welcomes any discussion about the future of the caucus. “I’m proud of what we’ve accomplished together — 55 seats and counting is an amazing result — and I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic Leader,” Schumer said. “I look forward to leading our new Democratic majority and delivering for the American people.” Divisions over Schumer have simmered over the last two years While Schumer is the favorite to win, Van Hollen’s run exposes a rift in the party that opened in the spring of 2025 , when Schumer was put on the defensive after he sided with Republicans on a spending vote. Even as Schumer has redeemed himself within his caucus since then — leading them through a government shutdown last year and orchestrating huge wins in the election — many in the Democratic base are agitating for generational change. Van Hollen, 67, is not that much younger than Schumer, 75. But he has positioned himself as a new face in the party. He has also said he is considering a run for president. While most Democratic senators have either said they are supporting Schumer or are undecided, Van Hollen has at least two backers: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, who won a competitive election in his state last week, and progressive standard bearer Bernie Sanders . El Sayed posted on X Thursday night that their majority will need “bold leadership.” “I called on Sen. @ChrisVanHollen to lead our caucus as a candidate back in April because he leads with courage and experience,” El-Sayed wrote. “We need both right now. Which is why I’m proud to stand with him in his bid to lead our Senate majority.” Sen. Sanders, an independent who caucuses with the Democrats, held a press conference Tuesday announcing he would not support Schumer. He posted Thursday night that the American people “want a Democratic Party that will stand up to powerful special interests, take on the billionaire class and fight for working families. That is why I am supporting Senator Chris Van Hollen to lead Senate Democrats.” Van Hollen has not yet laid out his own agenda, but he has criticized Schumer for his ties to Israel and other special interests. While Schumer has a long history of support for Israel, he has strongly criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his handling of the war in Gaza. Schumer says he has broad support Several senators have said they are backing Schumer, including incoming Ohio Sen. Sherrod Brown , who beat Republican Sen. Jon Husted last week. Beyond the election wins, those who support him say being the leader is a difficult job, experience is necessary and Schumer has proven himself with legislative successes when they held the Senate under President Joe Biden. “Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?” posted Maine Sen. Angus King, another independent who caucuses with Democrats and votes in the leadership election. “Chuck Schumer is one of the principal architects of the most successful election in modern history, and I see no reason to change the leadership that helped make that success possible,” King wrote. Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto, D-Nev., also posted her support Thursday evening: Cortez Masto said Schumer was key in “securing a historic majority. I will be supporting him as our Democratic leader.” This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/sen-chris-van-hollen-maryland-020344480.html

item.title: Police probe possible homeowners' association dispute after deadly D.C. shooting
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
At least four people were wounded and one was killed during a shooting at a condo building in the Logan Circle neighborhood of Washington, D.C., early Thursday, police said. The gunman was identified as 55-year-old emergency room physician Matt Lambert. Officers responded to reports of an active shooting at a gym inside the building just before 8 a.m. ET, Metropolitan Police Department interim chief Jeffery Carroll said at a press briefing. Once inside, police located one victim — building manager James Stuart, 46 — who died at the scene, Carroll said. Four others were wounded after Lambert went back up to his apartment, where he barricaded himself inside, and shot them from his balcony. They were transported to local hospitals. One was in critical condition, Carroll said. Three had non-life-threatening injuries. Much of the block was cordoned off, and nearby schools were placed on temporary lockdown. SWAT officers walk behind police tape at the scene of Thursday's shooting. AP Photo/Tom Brenner While police attempted to negotiate with Lambert, he fatally shot himself, Carroll said. While inside his apartment, Lambert also cut a natural gas line to the fireplace, starting a fire, Carroll said. The building's sprinkler system was activated and the fire was extinguished. Lambert's long-running disputes with his building's homeowners association are believed to be what prompted the attack, Carroll said, specifically with regard to "maintenance issues, mold and the like." He had ongoing litigation, claiming that his home was unlivable and that the problems began after a contractor had worked on the building's facade. He also appeared to share his problems on social media, saying in on post on X, "My manifesto is an engineering report." The building's management has denied responsibility. Joel Braithwaite, the lawyer who represented Lambert in the dispute, expressed shock at what happened, describing Lambert as someone who cared about people and was "calm and collected." "I'm at a loss for how things took any sort of turn that would have us here today," he told NBC 4 , adding, "Litigation wears on you." Law enforcement officers are seen atop a building in Washington, D.C., on Thursday following reports of an active shooting. AP Photo/Julia Demaree Nikhinson James Spellman, who was at the gym, told the Associated Press that there were about 50 people there when the shooting began. "Within seconds there was a man who fell to the ground, and a pool of blood came out," Spellman said. "One gym member rushed to help him. He was instantly dead. He had been shot in the neck." Witness Ryan Dubicki said he was in his apartment around 8 a.m. when he "heard about five bangs." "They were really spread out so I thought it was construction," Dubicki told the AP. His building's managers sent a notice about a possible active shooter. Another witness, Max Smith, told reporters that he heard gunshots and took shelter in a nearby shop. "I'm very shaken up," Smith said. "You know, you don't expect it." The shootings, which occurred just a mile from the White House, prompted a massive law enforcement response. Federal agencies, including the FBI and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, said they sent agents to the scene to help. item.title: Nvidia executive Ian Buck leads as CEO frontrunner on prediction markets
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
With Jensen Huang out as CEO at Nvidia ( NVDA ) and CFO Colette Kress taking on the role of interim CEO, Wall Street, the company's partners, and its customers are waiting to find out who the next permanent CEO will be. There are a number of candidates inside and outside of the company who could fill the position. But prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket have zeroed in on Nvidia VP of hyperscale and high-performance computing Ian Buck as the company's next leader. Both sites rank the odds of Buck taking over at roughly 40%. Buck has worked at Nvidia for the last 22 years, rising from a systems engineer to his current role as the head of the company's biggest businesses. The executive also has the kind of engineering chops that Nvidia's board may find compelling for the CEO role. Buck has a Ph.D. from Stanford University in computer science and, more importantly, developed Nvidia's CUDA technology. Nvidia's Vice President of hyperscale and high-performance computing Ian Buck poses for a photo in an unknown location. Nvidia/Handout via REUTERS Reuters / REUTERS CUDA allows companies to use the chip giant's graphics processing units (GPUs) for general computing, a capability that was instrumental in turning Nvidia into the AI powerhouse it is today. But Buck has a hard act to follow. Huang's charismatic personality drew customers and investors, turning him into one of the tech industry's biggest stars. And his penchant for elaborate keynotes at massive venues, where he regularly offered technical deep dives, drew thousands of attendees. It's unclear if any other executive could check all of the same boxes. For now, Wall Street analysts see Kress as a steady hand to guide Nvidia through the current storm. KeyBanc Capital Markets analyst John Vinh wrote in a note to investors that Kress's appointment as interim CEO is constructive "given her tenure as CFO since 2013 and deep institutional knowledge of Nvidia's business and strategy." Whoever Nvidia's board eventually chooses to lead the company will have plenty of questions to answer about its future and whether it can continue to dominate the industry as it did under Huang. item.title: Hegseth honors guard who scolded his group at the Tomb of Unknown Soldier
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Thursday honored the Army sentinel who forcefully scolded members of his entourage for laughing and talking near Arlington National Cemetery's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on Veterans Day. Hegseth posted a photo of himself on social media pinning a Joint Service Commendation Medal on the unidentified soldier's chest. "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist," Hegseth wrote. "Carry on Patriots." On Veterans Day, Hegseth, his wife Jennifer, and three of his top deputies were seen posing for photographs on the steps overlooking the tomb, which has provided a final resting place for several of America's unidentified service members — and a site of reflection and mourning — since 1921. Members of the group could be heard chuckling and chatting as they ascended the steps. We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist. Carry on Patriots. pic.twitter.com/Uk6ek6oOso — Secretary of War Pete Hegseth (@SecWar) November 12, 2026 The sentinel — a member of the Army's 3rd Infantry Regiment, known as The Old Guard — stepped forward and shouted in their direction: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!" Video of the encounter, which followed the annual Veterans Day wreath-laying ceremony, spread quickly online. A soldier guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier issued a verbal reprimand to a group of advisers and staffers with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth following a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery. As the group broke from taking photos, a loud laugh could be… pic.twitter.com/dIPp8wMGEG — The Associated Press (@AP) November 11, 2026 On Wednesday evening, Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell issued a statement saying the soldier had acted appropriately. "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Parnell said. Joint Service Commendation Medals are awarded to members of the Armed Forces who distinguish themselves while serving in a joint activity or on joint military staff. Hegseth's Veterans Day flap follows his brush with impeachment earlier this week . On Tuesday, the Republican-controlled U.S. House of Representatives voted to effectively kill the articles of impeachment against Hegseth — for now — by blocking their consideration on the House floor and sending them back to the Judiciary Committee, where GOP leaders can hold them up until the next Congress is seated in January 2027. Rep. Thomas Massie, a Republican from Kentucky, reintroduced impeachment charges against Hegseth on Monday, alleging that the embattled Pentagon chief had committed "high crimes and misdemeanors" and abused the power of his office by violating the War Powers Resolution, conducting military operations without congressional authorization and ordering unlawful military actions in several countries. Democrats — who voted unanimously against shelving the impeachment charges — will have a large House majority next year after winning at least 255 seats in last week's midterm elections. They have already vowed to try to remove Hegseth from office when they take control of Congress, building on voter dissatisfaction with the war in Iran. "In the majority, one of the first things we're gonna do is run Pete Hegseth out of town," Democratic Rep. Hakeem Jeffries of New York, the minority leader who is poised to become House speaker, said at a rally last month . Hegseth would be just the third Cabinet official in U.S. history to be impeached , and the second in three years. item.title: Microsoft Outlook outage drags on for hours as attempts to restore service fail
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
A widespread outage involving Microsoft's Outlook email and other applications stretched into Friday morning as the company said it was working to restore service. The tech giant first posted a statement on social media saying it was "investigating reports of users experiencing issues" accessing online mailboxes shortly before 1 p.m. ET Thursday. Downdetector , which monitors outages, reported issues with Outlook, Teams and other products on Thursday, as Microsoft attempted to deploy several fixes. Los Angeles International Airport tower hit by power outage The company has been providing updates on steps to resolve the outage on its Microsoft 365 Status social media account , providing a window into the hourslong effort to troubleshoot the disruption. In a post shortly after 11:30 p.m. ET , the company said it was working on efforts to improve server stability to improve traffic flow. "We're observing partial recovery across regions in which we've applied these adjustments; however, these actions aren't resulting in sustained recovery, so we're reviewing what additional actions we can take to improve overall infrastructure stability," the post stated. Earlier in the day, the company said: "We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact. We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service." Adobe Stock - PHOTO: Microsoft 365 apps. Around 6 p.m. ET Thursday, the company said it was "returning a portion of affected servers to the service, and they remain stable so far," though later updated that the servers "can become unresponsive again once they receive traffic" and was working on a fix for that. California fire crews save Little League game from power outage Earlier, Microsoft also reported some users were experiencing issues with Microsoft Teams. The company shortly updated that "mitigative actions have successfully restored service health and functionality." Amid the outage, New York City's Emergency Management Department warned residents of potential delays in reaching city agencies. "If you are trying to contact a New York City agency by email or access an online City service that relies on Microsoft systems, you may experience delays or temporary disruptions," NYC Emergency Management said on social media. "These issues may affect the delivery of emails, responses from City agencies, and access to certain online services." For more urgent requests, the city advised residents to try using an alternative method to contact the agency, and to call 311 for non-emergency city services and 911 for emergencies. This is a developing story. Please check back for updates. This article originally appeared on ABC News at https://abcnews.com/US/outlook-down-microsoft-outage-reported-mail/story?id=138088203

item.title: Senate Banking Committee chair calls on Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick to testify
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
By David Shepardson WASHINGTON, Nov 12 - US Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott sent letters on Thursday to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Nvidia's former ‌CEO Jensen Huang asking them to testify over recent developments at the company. Huang ‌stepped down from Nvidia, one of the major engines behind the AI boom, after reports of a romantic relationship ​with a businesswoman named Alice Huang whom US authorities suspect of spying for the Chinese government. In addition, a growing number of lawmakers have criticized Lutnick for the administration's refusal to add dozens of Chinese companies to a key US trade blacklist, and over whether the government ‌was properly overseeing Nvidia's exports ⁠to China. "Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," Scott wrote on X. "I am ⁠requesting that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee." Spokespeople for Huang and Lutnick could not immediately be reached. Scott said he would consider subpoenaing Huang ​if he ​does not voluntarily appear. "The American people deserve answers," ​Scott said. Senior White House officials were ‌separately discussing whether Lutnick should be pushed out, two people familiar with the situation said, as the desire to take action rose across Washington. Separately, the chairs of three House committees, including the head of the Foreign Affairs panel, Brian Mast, wrote to Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter, requiring them to appear for closed-door transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2, ‌respectively, or face subpoenas to compel their appearances. "There ​are clear national security concerns that need to be ​addressed immediately," Mast, as well as ​House China Select Committee Chair John Moolenaar and House Intelligence Committee ‌Chair Rick Crawford, wrote in the letter. They ​also asked Under Secretary ​of Commerce Jeffrey Kessler to testify at a December 3 hearing. China has denied Alice Huang is a spy and US Attorney General Todd Blanche said on ​Thursday that the Justice Department ‌has not yet reached a conclusion on whether she is or not. ​Alice Huang could not be reached for comment. (Reporting by Jasper Ward and David ​Shepardson in Washington; editing by Lincoln Feast.) item.title: SpaceX is trying to solve a decades-old challenge: Making rockets fully reusable
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
SpaceX's Starship Flight 14 launches at Starbase in Texas on September 28, 2026 (RONALDO SCHEMIDT) Elon Musk's SpaceX was poised Friday to carry out its latest test of the world's biggest and most powerful rocket, the Starship, with plans for a groundbreaking "catch" of the spaceship following a day in orbit. A successful capture of the Starship upper stage would mark a significant milestone in the space industry's decades-long pursuit of fully reusable spacecraft that can drastically reduce mission costs and make frequent travel possible. "If successful, this will mark the first full recovery of an orbital launch system and a breakthrough moment in making Starship a reliable, rapidly reusable rocket," SpaceX said. For the 15th Starship test flight Friday, SpaceX aims to recover both stages of the massive 124-meter (407-foot) launch vehicle. The company has caught the booster, dubbed Super Heavy, on three previous occasions, with the first stage descending vertically back to the launch site shortly after blastoff and nestling into mechanical "chopstick" arms. It will now attempt to do the same with the spaceship. Some versions of the vessel are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while others will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. A spacecraft that can be fully reused is the "Holy Grail" of the space industry, said Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies. "No one's really been able to do that so far," he said. "People have been trying to do that since the (NASA) space shuttle. But the space shuttle ended up being kind of a compromise because a lot of the vehicle wasn't reusable." Reusing the Starship spacecraft would require the vessel to withstand the extreme heat of reentering Earth's atmosphere and then return to service without extensive refurbishment. - Refueling challenge - Musk, the world's richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which are regularly employed to launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station. The Starship project, however, has been plagued by years-long delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges -- even as NASA is counting on the spaceship to serve as a lunar lander for its Artemis program. Other technical challenges include transferring fuel to Starship in orbit -- a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars. Following SpaceX's high-profile stock market debut in June, the company carried out the first orbital flight of Starship in September, though the mission was cut short due to an engine issue. It is also investing heavily in additional launch sites for its mega-rocket in Louisiana and Florida. - Complex capture - Friday's launch is scheduled to take place at SpaceX's "Starbase" in southern Texas at 4:45 pm (2245 GMT). Following liftoff and the mid-air separation of the two stages, SpaceX plans to bring Super Heavy back to Earth six and a half minutes later, catching it at the launch site on the Gulf of Mexico coastline. The spaceship will continue to reach Earth's orbit, where it will deploy 26 satellites into Musk's Starlink satellite internet constellation that has become a major revenue stream for SpaceX. It will then circle the planet 14 times, before returning 22 hours later and -- SpaceX hopes -- descending safely into the chopstick arms. This capture attempt is more complex than that of the booster, as the spaceship will be descending much faster and from a much greater altitude. SpaceX has said it would proceed with these maneuvers only if conditions are optimal, and in the past has made last-minute changes to test flights under Musk's "fail fast" strategy of learning through crashes, explosions and other mishaps. As of late Thursday, the US Federal Aviation Administration had not yet given its final approval for the test flight. cha-acb/mjf This article originally appeared on AFP at https://tech.yahoo.com/science/articles/spacex-starship-test-attempt-first-035915093.html

item.title: 'How does a building just fall?' Neighbors grieve after Brooklyn building collapse.
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
What we know about the New York City building collapse Over the loud noise of her radio, Ann Marie did not hear the sound of the Brooklyn building behind her home collapse on Wednesday night, but she soon saw the flashing lights of fire department trucks rushing to the scene. When she made her way out to the wreckage, workers were still searching for bodies. One of the building's walls had torn off, exposing the inside of several apartment homes, and the rubble had collapsed into a construction site next door. At least eight of her neighbours died in the accident - six adults and two children, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said. Five of the victims were residents, CBS reported. "Right now, I'm really scared," Marie told the BBC. "Now that I'm seeing exactly this side of the building, you can imagine the fright of those people, what happened to them." On Thursday afternoon, Mamdani said he had visited survivors in hospital. Eighteen people were injured, including four firefighters. One person is in critical condition. "I want to take a moment to remember those we have so senselessly lost," Mamdani added. "These were our friends and our neighbours, parents and children, young families building their lives in our city, immigrants from Mexico, Colombia, Trinidad and beyond." What we know about Brooklyn building collapse that killed eight people Later on Thursday, a senior official with the New York Police Department identified the victims as Nicole Daniela Salvada Rodriguez, 9, Juan Daniel Salvada Guzman, 31, Kevin Santiago Reyes Gonzalez, 10, Barry Mamadou, 23, and Ndiaye Mamadou, 31, according to CBS. They were residents of the building that collapsed. The other three victims lived elsewhere. Gabriel Siguencia, 22, lived in the Bronx, Edgar Sapon, 26, lived in Hell's Kitchen and Jose Luis Caguana Cosquillo, 26, lived in the Bushwick neighbourhood of Brooklyn. It was around 16:00 EST (21:00 GMT) on Wednesday when residents heard a loud boom as the 1930s building collapsed into a neighbouring construction site, where crews were working, according to fire department officials. Two construction workers were among the dead. The New York City Fire Department was on the scene within one minute of the emergency call, Mamdani said. Patricia Starek was waiting for her son to come home from school last night when she saw the helicopters near her home. The surge of the emergency responders initially brought back memories of New York during 2001 terrorist attacks. She has lived in Flatbush for 26 years, including during 9/11. "How does a building just fall into a pit? We all live here with the assumption that stairs are stable, floors are stable, that you can be on your third floor and not have the earth fall below you," she said. Mamdani said search conditions would grow more difficult with the rain in the morning, and responders continued their efforts for about 24 hours before determining on Thursday afternoon that there were no more victims at the site. Workers looked through the wreckage with drones, sniffer dogs, cranes and other equipment. Officials had said they would continue to search the wreckage until they were entirely certain there was no one left trapped, saying they still had big pieces of debris to remove. The mayor said city officials had identified the companies running the construction site, and were examining 100 other sites operated by the same groups to ensure they are safe. "His wife was very hysterical," said Kerr, who has lived in the neighbourhood since she was a teenager. "She couldn't take the pain." She said another man had been frantically going to all the nearby hospitals to try to find his two nephews, but still had no answers. Footage showed another woman who was six-months pregnant being rescued from the rubble. "She is alive. She is still alive. I'm very happy. I'm very happy," her husband told the BBC's US partner CBS News. "I thank all of you guys." [BBC] Starek, the longtime Flatbush resident, said she was heading to the local YMCA where some family members were gathered to see if she could help - and many others in the neighbourhood were doing the same. "People look out for each other," Marie said. To lose eight of her neighbours, she said: "I can't believe it. There's a pain." Kerr said she hoped her hours with the victims' families brought them some measure of comfort after one of the deadliest building collapses in recent New York history. "It's going to be very profound," she said of the impact the accident will have. "Hopefully this will bring the community together." item.title: No charges for driver in Kansas soccer field incident that killed 2 people
item.description:
Source: Yahoo Top Stories (World)
The crash on Oct. 17 in Wichita killed a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man and injured 10 others. (Wyatt Glosson/KAKE / AP) A woman who killed two people, including a 6-year-old boy, when she drove through a Kansas soccer game last month had taken a nap in her parked vehicle before it accelerated and won’t be criminally charged, officials said Thursday. The crash on Oct. 17 at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita killed a 6-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man, and injured 10 others when the vehicle drove through onto a soccer field at around 3:30 p.m. “I can not only find no evidence of an intentional crime, I can find affirmative evidence that there was not an intentional crime,” Sedgwick County District Attorney Marc Bennett said at a news conference. An off-duty police officer and others went to the truck after it had crashed and found the 34-year-old driver crying, Bennett said. The woman has not been publicly identified. “What they found was a sobbing, at turns described as frantic, hysterical, saying ‘I’m sorry, I’m sorry, what have I done,’ — words to that effect,” Bennett said. He said the accounts of the people who were there that day said “she was sleepy, looked like she had just woken up, these are comments from witnesses who arrived there at the door and interacted with her.” The woman got up around 6 a.m. and drove her husband’s truck from Garden City, around 200 miles away, to the sports complex where her children had games, officials said. She was not in her usual vehicle because hers had issues with tire air pressure, Sullivan said. Bennett and Wichita Police Chief Joe Sullivan called it a tragedy that has shaken the community. Sullivan said the investigation was thorough and fact-driven, and that “every lead was examined, every piece of evidence was reviewed.” “I also want to be honest with our community: There are some questions we may never be able to answer with complete certainty,” he said. Among them was whether the pickup was in park. The driver told her kids she was going to take a nap, and reclined the seat, Sullivan said. One child went to warm up for a game and the second, a 14-year-old, put a sunshade over the windshield so people couldn’t look in on the sleeping mother, officials said. Somehow the vehicle then accelerated and drove straight onto the soccer field. The truck was parked in a stall, with a 7-inch curb in front, with a straight line toward a sideline area, Bennett said. Investigators explored whether the woman may have been asleep and moved in her sleep and put the vehicle from park into drive. Bennett said that’s possible but unlikely because the foot would need to be on the brake to change gears and there would be other steps, and the gear shift is loud. The other scenario is that the truck was not placed in park and she did not realize it, and later accelerated, he said. Police did a recreation with a similar make and model, and an officer of similar proportions of the driver, and in that test the truck — while in drive — rested at the curb but did not go over, Bennett said. “Her child does say at one point she kind of turns, goes from her back to her side,” he said. “And if her foot comes forward and hits that accelerator, that’s all that has to take place for that to be the explanation.” Bennett made no judgments about what occurred, but said that criminal recklessness also wouldn’t apply in the case because that standard includes someone consciously disregarding a substantial risk. The woman told police that she believes she put the vehicle in park, Bennett said. One of the children said their mother went to sleep, and “next thing they know, the truck is leaping forward,” he said. “Mom says she wakes to, her kids are screaming, she looks up, she’s disoriented, she’s trying to sit up from a completely relaxed position to sit forward,” Bennett said. “Reaches for the steering wheel, looks up, sees shades that were not there when she went to sleep, batting at them.” The driver was cooperative and voluntarily gave blood after the crash, which tested negative for any intoxicating substances, Sullivan said. Police also examined her medical records, reviewed her social media, and had a General Motors engineer and technician examine the vehicle for any mechanical failures after the crash, Sullivan said. No mechanical problems were found, and the vehicle was not under any recalls, he said. The woman and her children had been at the complex most of the day, arriving in the morning, police said. Refs, coaches, and other people there were interviewed and no one reported any conflicts, Bennett said. “No one had a problem with this woman,” he said. Cole Adrian, 6, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, both of McPherson, Kansas, were killed. They were not related. The families of the victims and those injured were contacted by police and the district attorney’s office to inform them of the findings. He and Bennett said that the crash was a tragedy that has shaken the whole community. “There are families, friends, witnesses, first responders and members of this community who will forever carry the weight of that day,” Sullivan said.
